text:
Recent work supports separating recency, popularity and temporal availability. [Measuring Recency Bias (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) introduces a recency-bias metric and reports improvements after mitigating excessive recent-item emphasis. [Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns (RecSys 2025)](https://recsys.acm.org/recsys25/accepted-contributions/) compares random shuffling with constrained shuffling that respects items’ first observed availability: apparent sequential structure can reflect item availability, user behavior, or both. [TCA4Rec (2025)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40537-025-01184-9) addresses popularity dominance through asymmetric contrastive supervision; it provides motivation for frequency controls, rather than a validated frequency-matched diagnostic protocol.

The searches did not identify a directly matching 2024–2026 BERT4Rec protocol combining frequency-matched substitutions, positional controls and paired uncertainty. A proposed synthesis: replace recent versus older evidence with items matched on training frequency and availability; compare semantically similar versus dissimilar replacements using permitted titles/descriptions. Preserve sequence length, left padding, appended-mask position and candidate set. Separately swap recent and older items while preserving the exact item multiset; use local shuffles to distinguish recency placement from finer ordering. For repeated interests, distinguish repeated IDs from recurring semantic themes, checking first whether preprocessing retains duplicate interactions.

Measure paired changes in target–negative margins, target rank and HR@10; bootstrap users within category and report the macro-average change with uncertainty. These interventions measure model dependence, not causal user intent. Frequency bins alone do not establish a valid conditional-randomization test. Within one BERT4Rec model per category, resulting hypotheses could motivate recency-stratified masking, relative-position encoding, or popularity-aware loss experiments, selected through the unchanged validation evaluator.
